blogTitle: Earth inspired living:  The volcano and forest palettes down to earth colour trends
videoTitle: Down to Earth Colour Trends That Ground Your Space
script:
Down to Earth Colour Trends That Ground Your Space

Nature-inspired palettes — from rich volcanic reds to serene forest greens — can make your home feel grounded, calming, and deeply connected to the natural world.

Key takeaway: down-to-earth colour trends bring the calming essence of nature right into your living space — and studies show these shades genuinely reduce stress.

Volcano hues — rich reds, burnt oranges, glowing embers — bring a lively yet grounded energy that echoes the raw power found deep within the earth.

A deep terracotta wall balanced with soft cream textiles adds dynamism without overpowering the calm — perfect for a living room or home office where you want to spark creativity.

Reds and oranges trigger a strong emotional response — passion, warmth, vitality. Wisely paired with softer shades, they energise a space without overwhelming your senses.

A little tip I love: even a rusty red cushion or a terracotta rug is enough to introduce that volcanic warmth — you don't have to repaint a single wall.

Wall art is one of my favourite ways to bring volcano hues into a room — earthy tones blended with neutral tones anchor a space and add real personality.

Forest greens bring a quiet, soothing energy into your home — the kind that calms the mind and gently grounds your daily routine.

The soothing power of these down-to-earth tones is real — nature-mimicking colours have been shown to reduce stress and foster everyday mindfulness.

To balance forest greens, pair them with warm natural browns, muted creams, or soft sand tones — think linen, jute, unfinished wood, and woven baskets.

Texture is where things get really interesting — layering rough stone, woven linen, and earthy ceramics with your wall art creates warmth that goes well beyond colour alone.

For the right materials, think natural wood furniture, unglazed ceramics, raw linen, and woven jute — these all carry that honest, earthy quality that ties the whole palette together.

Bringing the outdoors inside is easiest with wall art — abstract prints that echo volcanic earth or forest depth instantly transform a plain wall.

To create a themed room, start with one anchor — a feature wall colour or a set of art prints — and let every other element (textiles, plants, ceramics) respond to it.

A cohesive themed room doesn't mean matching everything exactly — it means each piece feels like it belongs to the same natural world.

Combining volcano and forest elements is simpler than it sounds — try a forest green throw pillow alongside a volcanic orange vase and you've already got the balance working.

For a bolder statement, a deep volcanic red feature wall paired with leafy green plants and natural wood furniture creates that perfect push-and-pull between fire and forest.

Mindful design means being intentional — choose each piece because it genuinely adds warmth or calm, not just because it fills a gap.

Take care not to add too many bold tones at once — one or two earthy anchors with plenty of neutral breathing room will always feel more settled than a room full of competing colours.

Lighting matters more than most people realise — warm-toned bulbs or lantern-style fixtures amplify earthy tones beautifully and add an evening glow that feels genuinely cosy.

If you want a no-fuss way to bring earthy tones onto your walls, a set of 3 large prints in soft ivory and brown is a great place to start — no redecorating required.

Pro tip: start small. One art print, one plant, one earthy ceramic — you can always build from there once you see how the tones feel in your actual light.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
